title: Cancelling a ShieldCare Plan and What Comes Back
content:
## Clause 1: the customer's own authority

A cancellation of a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan is carried into the plan record only against a claim intake or change record
standing as signed by the customer for that plan. The signed record held against the plan is the
authority, correlated to the plan itself and settled before the cancellation is written.

## Clause 2: the free look

The whole premium is returned only when the cancellation is confirmed within the plan's free look
days, counted from the day the plan was activated. Free look days are counted as calendar days
from the activation day, which counts as day zero. The recorded activation day is the anchor and
the confirmation must fall no later than the last of those days; a confirmation on the last day is
inside the free look.

### Both sides of the free look

On a plan carrying 45 free look days, activated on day zero, a cancellation confirmed on the
forty-fifth day afterwards is inside the free look and a cancellation confirmed on the forty-sixth
is outside it. Calendar days are counted throughout.

## Clause 3: what a free-look cancellation returns

A cancellation confirmed inside the free look returns everything taken, including any
administration fee, and the plan is treated as never having been in force for premium purposes,
even though claims already paid are recovered from the refund.

## Clause 4: the state a refund may be booked on

A premium refund is booked only on a plan standing active, held while a claim is under review,
cancelled, or void.

## Clause 5: after the free look

After the free look, the plans that refund pro rata return the premium for the whole unused months
of the term, deduct every payout already made and the plan's administration fee, and pay nothing
where that leaves a negative figure. The plan whose basis gives no refund after the free look pays
nothing.

## Clause 6: a void plan

A void plan returns every premium taken with no administration fee deducted, because the plan was
never in force.

## Clause 7: where the money goes

A refund goes back to the method the premium was taken from where it is still on file, and
otherwise as store credit.

## A worked case on hypothetical figures

A plan taken for a single premium of 288.00 on a 24-month term is cancelled after 6 whole months have run,
on a basis that refunds pro rata; 400.00 of claims have already been paid and the plan's administration fee is
25.00. The premium for the 18 whole unused months is 216.00; the payouts already made and the administration
fee together come to 425.00; the refund is therefore nothing, because a pro rata calculation that leaves a
negative figure pays nothing.
